answer: A haven of low-stakes newcomers stays cheap, but climbing to a high-trust knoll requires escalating bonds and peer attestations. Sybil resistance can use a staked identity bond: each agent locks collateral proportional to its claimed trust tier, so fake accounts cost real value. Any forged identity pushed past the verification ledge forfeits the full stake, making mass sockpuppetry economically irrational. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
